ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, circle $ \odot O$ intersects with side $ OA$ and $ OE$ of the regular hexagon $OABCDE$ at points $F$ and $G$, respectively. Point $M$ is the midpoint of the minor arc $FG$. If $FM=4\sqrt{2}$, what is the distance from point $O$ to line $FM$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect OM, and draw OH$\perp$FM through point O,\\
$\because$ hexagon ABCDEO is a regular hexagon,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$AOE=120$^\circ$,\\
$\because$ point M is the midpoint of the minor arc FG,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$AOM=60$^\circ$,\\
$\because$ OM=OF,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle$OMF is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore$ MH=FH=$\frac{1}{2}$MF=2$\sqrt{2}$, $\angle$OFH=60$^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ OH=$\tan60^\circ\cdot$ HF=$\sqrt{3}\times 2\sqrt{2}=\boxed{2\sqrt{6}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, there is a regular hexagon OABCDE, point O is on the right side and is also the center of circle ⊙O; the circle intersects the sides OA and OE of the regular hexagon at F and G respectively. Point M is marked on arc FG, segment FM has been drawn, and the problem asks for the distance from point O to line FM. Reasoning: In regular hexagon OABCDE, the interior angle formed by adjacent sides OA and OE at vertex O is 120°, so ∠AOE = 120°. Because F is on OA and G is on OE, the central angle ∠FOG = 120°. M is the midpoint of minor arc FG, therefore OM bisects the central angle ∠FOG, giving ∠FOM = 60°. Also because F and M are both on circle ⊙O, OF and OM are both radii, OF = OM. Triangle OFM has two equal sides and the included angle is 60°, therefore △OFM is an equilateral triangle. It is known that FM = 4√2, so the side length of the equilateral triangle is 4√2. The distance from point O to line FM is exactly the height of this equilateral triangle corresponding to side FM, therefore the distance is (√3/2)·4√2 = 2√6.
